title: Kapre | Episode 1 [1 of 2] - If you smell cigar smoke under a balete tree

tts.note: Chatterbox clone of the user's chosen horror narrator MP3 (user says it is free to use)

lines.text: In the Philippines, if you smell cigar smoke under a big balete tree at night, *don't* look up.
And *never* say a bad word about that tree.
Because it's a *kapre*. A giant who lives in the old balete trees, smoking a cigar that never goes out.
Insult its tree, and it plays with you. You walk and walk, but every road leads back to the *same* tree.
That's why our lolas told us, say tabi tabi po when you pass. And if you get lost, turn your shirt *inside out*.
In 2009, my kuya Jun was sixteen.
He was walking home from a basketball game, past the old balete at the end of our road.
Then he smelled smoke. Sweet and heavy. Like a cigar.
He looked up, and saw a tiny red light, *high* in the branches.
Jun laughed. He kicked the roots and said, this ugly tree should be *cut down*.
The red light went *dark*.
He kept walking. Ten minutes later, he was back at the balete.
He turned around and went the other way. The balete. *Again*.
Three times. And every time, the smoke got *thicker*.
Then something laughed above him. Deep and slow, like the tree itself was laughing.
He remembered what Lola said.
So he pulled off his shirt, turned it inside out, and whispered, tabi tabi po. I'm *sorry*.
And just like that, he could see our porch light.
The next morning, on our doorstep, was a pile of grey *ash*.
Kuya Jun is thirty now. Last night, he called me at three a.m.
He said, I'm under the balete. I can smell the smoke.
And my shirt is *already* inside out.
